signal.name: Gemini Semantic Listening
signal.summary: The audio exhibits several characteristics of synthetic text-to-speech generation, including a flat, robotic cadence and a lack of natural breathing. There are noticeable metallic artifacts and unnatural phoneme transitions, particularly on the words 'reduce' and 'bags'. These factors strongly suggest the voice is AI-generated rather than a natural human recording.
signal.what_checked: Gemini listened for synthetic speech, cloned-voice artifacts, unnatural cadence, missing breathing, and generated-audio production patterns.
signal.what_found: The audio exhibits several characteristics of synthetic text-to-speech generation, including a flat, robotic cadence and a lack of natural breathing. There are noticeable metallic artifacts and unnatural phoneme transitions, particularly on the words 'reduce' and 'bags'. These factors strongly suggest the voice is AI-generated rather than a natural human recording.
signal.why_it_matters: When the dedicated wav2vec2 detector is missing or uncertain, Gemini gives the product a direct semantic audio review instead of stopping at an inconclusive model score.
signal.caveat: Gemini is an expert semantic judge, not a calibrated audio classifier. Treat this as one evidence signal in the trail.
observations: At 0:01, the word 'reduce' exhibits a robotic, flat pitch contour and unnatural phoneme transition.
Throughout the recording, there is an absence of natural breathing sounds or physiological pauses.
At 0:03, the word 'bags' ends with a metallic, synthetic resonance and an abrupt cutoff.

signals.name: Voice Authenticity Model
signals.summary: This audio appears to be AI-generated (TTS/voice cloning). Confidence: 93%. Inference via local wav2vec2.
signals.what_checked: A fine-tuned Wav2Vec2-XLSR transformer (160M params) was used to classify whether this audio was recorded from a real human voice or synthesised by a text-to-speech / voice cloning system (ElevenLabs, Amazon Polly, Kokoro, etc.).
signals.what_found: The model classified this audio as a AI-generated voice with 93% directional confidence. Probability real: 7% | Probability fake: 93%.
signals.why_it_matters: AI voice cloning is increasingly used to fabricate statements by public figures. This check catches spectral artifacts in the audio that TTS models leave behind.
signals.caveat: The model was fine-tuned on 6 TTS engines. Novel cloning systems not in its training set may evade detection. Short clips (<2.5 s) or heavily compressed audio may reduce accuracy.

signals.name: Acoustic Micro-Signature
signals.summary: The voice shows natural micro-variation (jitter 4.44%, shimmer 24.81%), consistent with real vocal-fold behaviour.
signals.what_checked: We measured the physical micro-variation of the voice: pitch jitter, amplitude shimmer, harmonic-to-noise ratio, and spectral tonality.
signals.what_found: The voice shows natural micro-variation (jitter 4.44%, shimmer 24.81%), consistent with real vocal-fold behaviour.
signals.why_it_matters: Real vocal folds never repeat a cycle perfectly. Text-to-speech and voice clones tend to be smoother and more regular, so this measured signature is hard for a generator to fake without modelling true vocal physics.
signals.caveat: Heavy compression, noise reduction, and short or noisy clips can distort these measurements, so this is weighed with the other audio signals.
observations: Real human speech carries small, irregular variation from cycle to cycle. Synthetic and cloned voices are often smoother and more regular than a real vocal tract.
